source_text: Common forms include Type I (clitoridectomy, removing the clitoral prepuce and/or glans) and Type II (excision, removing the clitoris and labia minora, sometimes with labia majora trimming), with rarer instances of Type IV variants like symbolic nicking or scraping; these are typically conducted by traditional practitioners on infants or girls under 15 using unsterilized tools, leading to immediate risks of hemorrhage, infection, and shock, alongside long-term complications such as chronic pain, urinary and menstrual disorders, sexual dysfunction, and obstructed labor increasing maternal and neonatal mortality.
